title: Probabilistic pad pruner: prefill-aware microbatch trimmer with kernel hinting
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Currently our prefill + decode pipeline groups requests by coarse sequence-length buckets which reduces padding but still leaves tail-heavy waste for bursty workloads. This increases token cost and can harm p99 latency when long requests force kernel choices suboptimal for the majority of short-prefill workloads. This ticket introduces a probabilistic pad pruning step in the prefill path that trims microbatch padding edges with a safety policy, and surfaces kernel hint metadata to the kernel selector so it can choose more appropriate kernels for the trimmed microbatch. The goal is to reduce padded tokens without increasing error rates or visible truncation for customers.
technical_design: 1) During prefill batching we compute per-batch length histogram and identify the top 90th percentile cutoff length. 2) For requests longer than cutoff we don't trim; for requests shorter we compute an eviction probability proportional to the per-request distance from the cutoff (sigmoid-scaled) and sample a boolean to tentatively mark trailing pad tokens as removable. 3) For each microbatch we attach kernel_hint metadata: {preferred_kernel: fast-small, expected_max_seq: N_trimmed, require_full_kv: false}. This metadata flows to the kernel selection layer which runs a low-cost compatibility check before binding a kernel. 4) We add a safety validator: if any trimmed microbatch would cause prefills to exceed a token budget or reduce model logits stability beyond a threshold (measured by a short emulation step), revert trimming for that batch. 5) Integrate metrics: trimmed_pad_tokens, backoffs_reverted, kernel_hint_matches, p50/p95/p99 latency by bucket. Implementation is in three parts: batching layer changes (Go), kernel hint API (Rust/C++), and a small validation harness in Python for regression checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end integration merges to canary and passes the safety validator in 95% of synthetic runs.
- Trimmed padded tokens reduced by >=25% on tail-heavy synthetic trace and >=8% on customer-like traces.
- No regression in token-level generation quality measured by our eval harness (mean logit distance < 0.003).
- p99 latency for short-prefill workloads improves or stays within 3% of baseline.
- Kernel selector consumes kernel_hint metadata and prefers small-kernel variant when compatible in >=80% of applicable batches.
tasks: Design probabilistic eviction function and tune hyperparameters
Add pad-prune flags and per-request sampled decision in prefill packer (Go)
Define kernel_hint proto and wire to kernel selection API (Rust)
Implement safety emulator that simulates trimmed prefill for a sample of batches (Python)
Add metrics and tracing to observe trim decisions and reverts
Create canary config and rollout plan
Run synthetic and customer-like trace experiments and collect results
Document feature and add SDK notes about potential kernel hints
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Trimming could cause logits divergence for models sensitive to prefix context. Mitigation: conservative default probability, safety emulator, and automatic revert with alerting. Risk: Kernel hint mismatch could cause incompatible kernel selection causing runtime errors. Mitigation: kernel selector must always perform compatibility handshake and fall back to baseline kernel. Risk: Increased CPU work for validation may harm throughput. Mitigation: sample only 1-2% of batches for full emulation in prod; use cheap approximations elsewhere.
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction math and sampling, integration test for kernel_hint propagation, canary job that replays production traces with and without trimming, regression tests using the eval harness to assert logit distance thresholds. Performance e2e to collect tokens trimmed, latency by bucket, and kernel selection match rate.
proposed_rollout: 1) Feature gate off by default. 2) Internal canary (10% of infra) for 48h on non-customer-critical traffic. 3) If stable, expand to 50% and run 72h with monitoring. 4) Gradual wider rollout to 100% with options for per-customer opt-out. Rollback plan: flip gate off and revert kernel_hint consumers; alerting for >1% revert rate.
metrics_and_targets: trimmed_pad_tokens: -25% (synthetic), -8% (customer-like); p99 latency change: <= +3% for short-prefill; kernel_hint acceptance: >=80%; backoff_revert_rate: <2% acceptable, >5% auto rollback

notes: This approach focuses on low-risk wins for short-prefill-dominant workloads. Follow-up work could include adaptive learning of eviction hyperparameters per-customer and tighter coupling with cost-optimization signals.
